headline: US markets finished strong last night on tech gains, oil dropped sharply on easing Middle East supply fears, and Google's new Gemini 4 Argon AI model is beating rivals at coding — good news for your GOOG holding.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG had a solid night last night, up 1.77% to $340.86 USD. The big driver is the launch of Google's new Gemini 4 Argon AI model, which benchmarks show beating OpenAI's GPT-6 and Anthropic's Claude at coding tasks. Markets are rewarding Google for showing it can genuinely compete at the AI frontier after a period of playing catch-up.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft climbed 0.89% last night to $517.35 USD. News that Microsoft posted a trillion-dollar quarter — driven heavily by its Azure cloud and AI business — reinforced confidence that the AI investment story is very much alive. Solid and steady.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a decent session today, closing up 1.37% to $3.70. There's no single big catalyst — it looks like a modest recovery bounce. The stock is still deep in the red overall (down ~45% on your cost base), so one good day doesn't change the bigger picture. Lithium sentiment remains fragile.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two was essentially flat last night, slipping just 0.13% to $203.36. No major news moved it. There's chatter that GTA 6 could push game prices even higher, which could be a long-term revenue tailwind for Take-Two as the publisher — but that's a story for down the track, not today.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: No price data available for today's ASX close — the ETF didn't trade or data wasn't captured. Last recorded price was $75.74. The underlying US markets it tracks finished strongly last night, so expect a positive lean when data resumes.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: No price data for today's session. Last close was $542.68. The S&P 500 and NASDAQ both rose solidly last night, so VTS should reflect that positively once pricing catches up.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: No price data for today's session. Last close was $94.41. China's move to halt fuel exports (see world news) is worth watching — it could create some short-term headwinds for emerging market sentiment, particularly Asia-heavy ETFs like this one.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: No price data for today's ASX close. Last recorded price was $17.41. Google's Gemini 4 Argon launch is a genuine positive for the AI sector broadly — this ETF should benefit from continued momentum in AI stocks globally.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Gemini 4 Argon launch is a real tailwind
watch_today.detail: Google's new Gemini 4 Argon model dropped this week and benchmarks show it beating both OpenAI's GPT-6 and Anthropic's Claude at coding. GOOG was already up 1.77% last night reflecting this. For a long-term holder, this is exactly the kind of development that strengthens the investment thesis — Google is proving it belongs at the AI frontier. Sit tight and feel good about this one.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Trillion-dollar quarter confirms the AI story is real
watch_today.detail: Microsoft's latest quarterly results showed a trillion-dollar revenue milestone, with Azure cloud and AI products doing the heavy lifting. The stock is up 16.75% on your cost base and keeps delivering. Nothing here suggests you'd want to sell — this is exactly what long-term buy-and-hold looks like. Hold confidently.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Small bounce, but the hole is still deep
watch_today.detail: Pilbara closed up 1.37% today to $3.70, which is a nice green day, but the stock is still down about 45% on your invested amount. Lithium prices remain soft globally and there's no structural change yet. For a long-term holder, the thesis depends on the lithium cycle turning — that hasn't happened yet. Hold and be patient, but don't expect a quick turnaround.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 price talk is a slow-burn positive
watch_today.detail: There's growing speculation that GTA 6 — Take-Two's biggest upcoming release — could set a new benchmark for game prices (potentially $100+ USD). If that lands well, it's a meaningful revenue boost for Take-Two. The stock is down 12% on your cost base, but the long-term case rests heavily on GTA 6's success. Nothing to do right now — just watch for release news.

watch_today.title: Middle East tensions: oil fell sharply, but watch for escalation
watch_today.detail: Crude oil dropped 3.24% last night to $89.86, partly because supply flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain intact despite Iranian threats. However, the US is sending a third aircraft carrier group to the Middle East and Trump is openly threatening new strikes on Iran. If the situation escalates, oil could spike hard — that would ripple through inflation and potentially delay RBA rate cuts. Keep an eye on this.

watch_today.title: RBA: CBA boss says rate hikes are probably done
watch_today.detail: The Commonwealth Bank CEO said this week he believes the RBA's rate hiking cycle is finished. If that's right, it's good news for growth assets like your ETFs and tech stocks — lower rates make future earnings worth more. The AUD also ticked up 0.44% last night, which slightly reduces the AUD value of your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) when converted back. Nothing dramatic, just worth knowing.

world.summary: The big global stories today centre on rising US-Iran tensions with a third US carrier group heading to the Middle East, oil markets reacting to the threat, China using fuel exports as geopolitical leverage, and multiple concerning moves around US election integrity ahead of the midterms.

stories.title: US sends third aircraft carrier to Middle East as Iran tensions escalate
stories.why_it_matters: The US is deploying a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East as President Trump openly threatens new military strikes on Iran and says Iran is 'ready to fold up.' Thousands of additional US troops are also being sent to the region. Iran has been threatening the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which about 20% of the world's oil flows. For everyday Australians, a serious escalation could push oil prices sharply higher, feeding back into fuel costs and inflation at the bowser.

stories.title: Oil prices drop 3% despite ongoing Strait of Hormuz threats
stories.why_it_matters: Despite the military build-up, crude oil actually fell 3.24% last night to $89.86 a barrel because oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz are currently holding up and markets think Iran won't actually block the waterway. This is a bit of a paradox — big military tension, but prices falling because the actual supply disruption hasn't materialised yet. It's a fragile situation: any real incident could flip oil sharply higher overnight.

stories.title: China halts fuel exports — is Beijing using energy as a geopolitical weapon?
stories.why_it_matters: China has paused its fuel exports, raising concern that Beijing is turning energy supply into a geopolitical bargaining chip — similar to Russia's use of gas supplies against Europe. The move could tighten global fuel markets and adds to the complexity of US-China tensions. For Australian investors, it's a reminder that emerging market exposure (like VGE.AX) carries geopolitical risk, and that commodity prices can shift quickly on policy decisions from Beijing.

stories.title: Trump doesn't rule out declaring a state of emergency before the US midterm elections
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump has refused to rule out declaring a national state of emergency before the US midterm elections, a move that legal experts say would be unprecedented and deeply concerning for democratic norms. Separately, his administration has abandoned efforts to investigate election threats, and a new lawsuit alleges his administration made it harder for US citizens living abroad to vote. A federal judge also struck down a key part of a noncitizen voting law the administration had been using. Taken together, these stories paint a picture of serious pressure on US electoral institutions heading into the midterms.

stories.title: Brazil probes US funding of far-right political causes
stories.why_it_matters: Brazil's government has called for an investigation into alleged US funding of far-right political groups within Brazil. The move signals growing friction between Brasília and Washington, and is part of a broader global trend of democracies pushing back against what they see as foreign interference in their domestic politics. Brazil is one of Australia's key trade and diplomatic partners in the Southern Hemisphere, and instability there matters for emerging market sentiment.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was a good one — both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ pushed higher, led by tech. The big standout was oil, which dropped over 3% as Middle East supply fears eased temporarily. Gold ticked up slightly and the Aussie dollar strengthened a touch. ASX 200 data wasn't captured for today's close.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Solid night last night — broad market gains driven by tech strength.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech led the charge last night, up 1.42%. Google's Gemini AI launch and Microsoft's earnings momentum both contributed.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: No data captured for today's ASX close. Last recorded level was 8,614.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell sharply last night — down 3.24% — as actual oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz remained intact despite US-Iran tensions. A volatile situation.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold nudged up slightly, reflecting some ongoing safe-haven demand amid geopolitical uncertainty.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar strengthened a little — traders are becoming more confident the RBA is done hiking rates, which paradoxically lifted the AUD as sentiment improved.

politics.summary: The RBA dominates Australian news this week — a rate hike has landed and now the debate is whether it's the last one. CBA's boss reckons the hiking cycle is over. Meanwhile, the Albanese government is pushing forward on AI legislation.

stories.title: CBA boss says RBA rate hikes are probably finished
stories.why_it_matters: Commonwealth Bank CEO Matt Comyn has said publicly that the Reserve Bank's interest rate hike cycle is 'probably finished.' This matters a lot for everyday Australians — if he's right, mortgage repayments should stop rising, and the pressure on household budgets from rate hikes eases. For investors, it's a signal that growth assets like shares and ETFs could get a tailwind, since lower rates make future company earnings more valuable.

stories.title: RBA denies staff a pay rise that keeps up with inflation — hours after hiking rates
stories.why_it_matters: In a move that has raised eyebrows, the RBA knocked back a staff pay rise that would have kept up with inflation — on the same day it raised interest rates. Critics argue this is hypocritical: the RBA is asking Australians to accept lower real wages to fight inflation, while not applying the same logic internally. It's already sparked union anger and a political debate about whether the RBA is out of touch.

stories.title: Albanese government pushes forward with AI legislation
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government says it is 'getting on with the job' of delivering AI legislation, positioning Australia as one of the first countries to put formal rules around artificial intelligence. The move is aimed at managing risks like AI-generated misinformation and bias in automated decisions, while keeping Australia competitive globally. For investors in AI-related stocks and ETFs like GXAI.AX, a clear regulatory framework — rather than a ban-first approach — is generally market-friendly.

stories.title: RBA cash rate hike flows through to savings accounts
stories.why_it_matters: Following the RBA's latest rate hike, several banks have passed on the increase to savings account rates. If you're holding cash on the sidelines, it's worth checking whether your savings account has been updated — some institutions are slower than others to pass on the full increase. Higher savings rates also slightly reduce the appeal of riskier assets like shares, as the 'safe' return on cash improves.

ai.summary: Google dominated AI headlines this week with the launch of Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful model yet — and benchmark results suggest it's genuinely beaten OpenAI and Anthropic at coding tasks. Meanwhile, the FTC is reportedly probing both OpenAI and Anthropic, even as the Trump administration favours letting the industry regulate itself.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon — beats GPT-6 and Claude at coding
stories.why_it_matters: Google has released Gemini 4 Argon, its most powerful AI model to date. Early benchmarks show it outperforming OpenAI's GPT-6 and Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 on coding tasks specifically. CEO Sundar Pichai said Google is moving to 'make AI work for everyone.' For holders of GOOG, this is a significant moment — Google has been seen as playing catch-up in the AI race, and this launch suggests it's now a genuine frontrunner. The model is not yet widely available to free-tier users.

stories.title: CNBC asks: does Gemini 4 Argon really compete at the frontier?
stories.why_it_matters: CNBC takes a sceptical look at whether Gemini 4 Argon truly matches the hype, noting that Google has previously announced models that underdelivered in real-world use. Benchmark wins are one thing, but day-to-day usefulness for developers and consumers is another. The article concludes the model is genuinely competitive but notes it remains out of reach for most free-tier users — so the commercial impact may take time to flow through.

stories.title: FTC reportedly probing OpenAI and Anthropic as Trump backs AI self-regulation
stories.why_it_matters: The US Federal Trade Commission (FTC — America's consumer protection and competition watchdog) is reportedly investigating both OpenAI and Anthropic, likely around competitive practices and data use. At the same time, the Trump administration is publicly backing a light-touch, self-regulation approach for the AI industry. This tension — regulators probing big AI companies while the White House says let them be — creates uncertainty for the sector, but broadly a 'regulate less' environment tends to be positive for AI company valuations.

stories.title: Australia moves toward formal AI legislation
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese government is progressing AI laws that would regulate how artificial intelligence is developed and deployed in Australia. The legislation is expected to focus on transparency, accountability, and preventing harmful automated decisions. It's a pragmatic, framework-first approach rather than an outright ban — which should keep Australia open for AI investment and innovation while setting guardrails. Good context for holders of GXAI.AX.

sport.summary: The NRL Grand Final is set — Roosters vs Knights at Accor Stadium on Sunday. AFL end-of-season moves and awards are dominating footy news. A big story on the 11 NRL stars retiring this season, and tennis' antitrust lawsuit rolls on.

stories.title: NRL Grand Final: Roosters vs Knights, Sunday 6:30pm at Accor Stadium
stories.why_it_matters: It's Grand Final week. The Sydney Roosters take on the Newcastle Knights at Accor Stadium this Sunday at 6:30pm. It's shaping up as a classic — the Roosters' big-game experience versus the Knights' fairytale run. Mark it in the calendar.

stories.title: 11 NRL stars retiring: a boxer, fashion designer, and the next Joe Rogan?
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports has profiled the 11 NRL stars calling it quits at the end of this season. Among the post-football plans: one is pursuing boxing, another is launching a fashion label, and a third is eyeing a podcast career in the mould of Joe Rogan. It's the end of an era for some genuine legends of the game — a nice human-interest read heading into Grand Final weekend.

stories.title: Bulldogs star lands new NRL club; Souths make call on ex-bad boy
stories.why_it_matters: The off-season player movement continues even during Grand Final week. A Bulldogs star has found a new NRL home for 2027, while the South Sydney Rabbitohs have made a contract decision on a player with a chequered past. The full details of the players involved weren't in the article text, but the transfer window is heating up fast.

stories.title: AFL end-of-season: Heeney's remorse, Fagan goes out on top
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL season is wrapping up and the post-mortems are rolling in. Isaac Heeney has spoken about his remorse following Sydney's finals exit, while Brisbane Lions coach Chris Fagan is reportedly going out on top after a successful tenure. The Sydney Swans also handed out their end-of-season awards. A big week for AFL fans reflecting on what was.

stories.title: Tennis antitrust lawsuit: judge refuses to dismiss case against ATP, WTA and Grand Slams
stories.why_it_matters: A US federal judge has refused to throw out an antitrust lawsuit (a legal challenge about unfair market control) against the ATP, WTA, and the four Grand Slam tournaments. The players bringing the case argue that tennis' governing bodies have an illegal monopoly over where and when pros can compete, and how prize money is set. If the case succeeds, it could fundamentally reshape how professional tennis is structured and how much players earn.
